findings.title: Material-sample comments promise stability across different collections
findings.evidence: local-invariants-host.log (local): #000000 alone -> Satin black; in [#000000,#000001,#000002,#FFFFFF,#FFFFFE] -> Matte racing green.
findings.reproduction: After pnpm build, run node docs/audits/AUD-007-harnesses/local-invariants.mjs. Compare chooseMaterialSamples("vehicle", ["#000000"]) with the same reference in the five-color list.
findings.expected: Comments describe deterministic assignment for a given collection and explain that adding other references can change its decorative sample.
findings.observed: Source says "The same reference always gets the same sample"; test says "whatever comes with it". Greedy one-to-one assignment depends on the full collection. The test checks reversal/case and duplicates, not changed neighboring references.
findings.impact: Misleading maintenance/test contract only. Exact printed hex references and QR payloads are unaffected, and the renderer supplies the whole collection when rendering a fragment. No recovery or confidentiality failure demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify both comments with the collection context; if cross-collection stability is intended, design that separately rather than changing the recovery representation.
findings.requiredVerification: Keep the counterexample and confirm full-sheet versus individual-fragment consistency for the same collection and exact payload preservation.

informationalNotes: The SSKR relocation has no confirmed functional or security defect. The Rust bridge is byte-unchanged by the relocation; its current toolchain/dependencies and generated WASM were independently rebuilt.

Dockerfile.sskr downloads x86-64 Node and rustup, but the production wrapper does not pass --platform linux/amd64. This audit used an explicit platform. Native ARM-host builds were not attempted; pin the canonical platform or document the x86-64 requirement before promising portable source builds.

The new build wrapper has useful marker/loader guards but no dedicated tests for missing markers, Docker failure, a one-byte rebuilt mismatch or preservation of tracked files in --check. Add audit-only/fake-Docker regression coverage if extending this script; the current real compare passed.

The existing AUD-005-BLD007 timing concern recurred on two card tests (one has its own 30 s timeout). Prefer bounded test concurrency over weakening assertions; current sequential rerun passed without raising limits.

ci.yml lacks its own concurrency group; executable.yml cancels in-progress runs including tag runs. Consider matching the workspace policy to cancel superseded verification while excluding publication from cancellation. No interrupted release was reproduced.
Removal of the network loader and hashes are integrity consistency checks, not signatures or protection against a host that can replace the application and manifest together.

remediation.evidence: src/export/material-artwork.ts and test/material-cards.test.ts now say that the same references get the same samples in any order and letter case, that neighbours take part in the choice, and that an individual fragment takes its sample from the whole card (material-cards.ts chooses once over content.colors and indexes it by entry). local-invariants.mjs still prints the counterexample and recovers 30 quorums with 20 rejections; test/material-cards.test.ts passes 20/20, including the individual-fragment test; no code, payload or vector changed.
Current workflow/source reviewed and Linux executable passes; current Windows/macOS GitHub execution still pending.
Current Linux notice scan passes with 17 npm packages. Platform-wide GitHub evidence still pending.
README distinguishes ordinary MNC1 output and SSKR share-file output; actual standalone SSKR split/recovery passes.

limitations: Overall release acceptance is INCOMPLETE: current Windows/macOS executable and CI runs and tag-time reusable CI/SSKR gate were not executed. No push, tag, release or publication was performed.

The unmodified default pnpm verify command did not finish green: 464/466 passed, two timeouts; the affected two files passed 38/38 sequentially. These are overlapping runs, not 502 distinct tests. Concurrent unrelated MHFE work was observed; causality is not proved by a passing rerun.

Fresh compilation was uncached only for the offline built stage. Pinned toolchain/dependency Docker layers were reused; the base image, compiler installation and registries were not rebuilt from scratch.

No native ARM build host, Windows or macOS execution, physical print/camera scan, assistive technology, manual secret TTY session, comprehensive memory forensics, malicious OS defense or independent cryptographic certification.
Full scope means every checklist area has a disposition, not exhaustive input/state coverage. Prior audit claims are context; only commands listed here were executed on this snapshot.
